title: Symbol Resolution and Symbol Tables
description: Explain how a linker turns a name into an address: binding, visibility, archive extraction, versioning and the symbols the linker invents on your behalf.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 12 concepts and reproduce the 84 measured checks in courses/sym/assets/samples/crosscheck.py

concepts.title: A Name Is Not a Symbol
concepts.description: The linker is asked one question over and over, and the question is not about names.

concepts.title: Binding, and the Two Tables
concepts.description: LOCAL, GLOBAL and WEAK, and why an object file carries two symbol tables instead of one.

concepts.title: Visibility Is Not Binding
concepts.description: Four visibility values, and the measured fact that two of them are not stored in the visibility field at all.

concepts.title: The Algorithm, Measured
concepts.description: What a linker actually does, left to right, driven by demand rather than by the order you wrote the files.

concepts.title: Order, Archives and the Map File
concepts.description: Why the order of two archives on the command line can decide whether your program links at all.

concepts.title: Two Definitions and One Tentative
concepts.description: Multiple definition, and the storage class that made the same source legal for thirty years.

concepts.title: Two Hash Tables, One Job
concepts.description: How the loader finds a name in constant time, and the counter-intuitive layout of the GNU table.

concepts.title: The PLT and the GOT
concepts.description: Six instructions that turn a call into a lookup, read one instruction at a time.

concepts.title: Lazy, Eager, and the Flag That Does Nothing
concepts.description: A dynamic-section flag, a symbol that is never called, and the experiment that separates the two binding times.

concepts.title: Who Owns the Storage
concepts.description: GLOB_DAT and COPY, and the code-model flag that silently decides which of them you get.

concepts.title: Versioned Symbols
concepts.description: Three tables, a parent chain, and a hash that is the same hash as the symbol table's.

concepts.title: Symbols the Linker Invents
concepts.description: The four boundary symbols, the section markers, and writing a resolver that agrees with ld.
